PCS' initial estimate of Hurricane Ida was $26bn. This has now moved out to approximately $27.5bn. Modelling firms' and financial analysts estimates range from $17bn to excess of USD 40bn. Most recently (Jan 2022) Munich Re has estimated Ida at $36bn. For context, these ranges make the loss significantly bigger than Irma which is currently at $27bn. Major Hurricane Ida has been our largest event.

Four individual events topped the $20bn threshold for economic loss for only the second time ever being Hurricane Ida, Flooding in Europe (Bernd), Summer flooding in China and the Polar Vortex in North America in February 2021. Exposure to other major events such as the major European Storms and Floods (Bernd) and Winter Freeze Uri have been modest.

gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 3.217 million in 2021, calculated from changes in cumulative gross claims incurred for underwriting years 2014-2019. This strengthening was influenced by the deterioration of COVID-19 related reserves from 2020 and natural catastrophe loss activity affecting the 2020 year of account, including Hurricanes Laura and Sally. Despite these adverse movements, the 2019 year of account closed with a profit.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2021 gross claims outstanding were GBP 157.079m. The report does not disclose a single aggregate quantified prior-year reserve movement amount; closed years 2014-2018 are reported as having "no material developments" while the syndicate highlights that 2021 experienced significant natural catastrophe activity (e.g. Hurricane Ida, European floods 'Bernd', China flooding, Polar Vortex) and continued pressure on US Casualty reserves. COVID-19 had a modest adverse effect and is noted as a slight deterioration on the 2020 Covid-related reserve. Overall the syndicate describes mixed reserve pressures: material catastrophe-driven upward pressure on property-related reserves and adverse development in US casualty, partially mitigated by releases/non-material movements on older closed years.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding is taken from the Technical Provisions note (explicit). No single quantified 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' figure is provided in the report; only narrative statements (e.g. 'no material developments' for closed years) and per-event mentions are given. Prior-year development therefore is not reported as a single number and has been left null. LOB reserve movements are inferred from narrative (confidence <1). Named events and causal phrases were extracted from the Underwriter and Managing Agent narrative sections.
